front.title: The Signed-Agent-Metadata HTTP Header Field for Web Bot Auth

abstract.t:
Web Bot Auth uses HTTP Message Signatures to let automated HTTP clients authenticate their identity to origins via the Signature- Agent header field. When a multi-tenant agent platform signs outbound requests with a shared key, all customer workloads on that platform share a single cryptographic identity. Abusive traffic from one tenant or workload can degrade the reputation of the entire platform and cause origins to block legitimate tenants.
This document defines the Signed-Agent-Metadata HTTP header field, an RFC 9651 Dictionary that carries optional, pseudonymous per-request metadata (product, project, and session). By signing Signed-Agent- Metadata inside the Web Bot Auth signature, a platform enables verifiers to evaluate traffic, apply rate limits, and isolate reputation at a narrower scope than the signing origin.
